items.title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
items.raw_text: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade. As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits. Solid-state models, in comparison, combine magnetic components with high-power semiconductors, making them more compact and allowing for more control over the flow of electricity. These devices are still in development, and can’t replace all traditional transformers today, especially the largest ones that work at the high voltages necessary for long-distance transmission. But a new generation of transformer technology could be a crucial part of our future grid. items.title: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms
items.raw_text: Consider what passes for success in technology policy. An AI company promises that its chatbot will not encourage suicide . A social media platform makes it more difficult for children to buy fentanyl . These are important protections, and they should have existed all along. But companies can clear these low bars while continuing to make products that leave young people dependent on simulated friendships or trapped in feeds built to keep them scrolling. We have historically allowed the debate over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. As we transition into an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than merely address catastrophic harms. We should take measures to ensure that its products don’t erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another. A teenager who develops an unhealthy attachment to an AI companion may never appear in a lawsuit or a newspaper, except in the most egregious cases. Neither will the student who begins relying on a chatbot to write every paper, or the young person who measures their life against a social media feed engineered to provoke envy and keep them watching. Worms mate in man's eyes, get plucked out right before larvae burst out
items.raw_text: After two months of discomfort, a man in South Korea went to an eye clinic where doctors pulled 11 living, wriggling worms from his eyes. They apparently made the most of their time on the man's peepers; at the time of extraction, many of the female worms were pregnant. The man narrowly avoided having them spew their loads of living larvae directly into his eyes. The man in this case was a 71-year-old crop farmer. He told doctors that for the previous two months he had the sensation of having something stuck in both his eyes, which were also red and blurry. When ophthalmologists took a look, they quickly saw the problem: multiple mobile, whitish roundworms. His eyes were not in good shape either, as one might expect. The blood vessels in the membrane over the eye, the conjunctiva, were enlarged, making his eyes look red. And the cells of his cornea—the transparent, dome-shaped outer layer of the eye—had eroded, potentially after the helminths' hanky-panky. According to a case report published in the New England Journal of Medicine , the doctors gave the man a topical treatment to numb his eyes and then began plucking out the worms one by one with fine forceps. items.title: Meet the real-life Scottish surgeon who inspired Sherlock Holmes
items.raw_text: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle created one of the most beloved fictional detectives of all time in Sherlock Holmes, spawning countless novels, films, TV series, and so forth featuring the sleuth. Far fewer people know about the real-life inspiration for Holmes: a renowned surgeon at Scotland's University of Edinburgh named Joseph Bell, who taught Doyle when the author was still a young medical student. Bell is the subject of a new, eminently readable biography, Sleuth-Hound: The Case of the Real Sherlock Holmes , by medical historian Lindsey Fitzharris. A noted science communicator with a fondness for the medically macabre, Fitzharris published a biography of Scottish surgical pioneer Joseph Lister, The Butchering Art , in 2017—a great, if occasionally grisly, read. She followed up with 2022’s The Facemaker: A Visionary Surgeon’s Battle to Mend the Disfigured Soldiers of World War I , about a WWI surgeon named Harold Gillies who rebuilt the faces of injured soldiers. In 2020, Fitzharris hosted a documentary for the Smithsonian Channel, The Curious Life and Death Of… , exploring famous deaths, ranging from drug lord Pablo Escobar to magician Harry Houdini. Fitzharris performed virtual autopsies, experimented with blood samples, interviewed witnesses, and conducted real-time demonstrations in hopes of gleaning fresh insights. Starting at $699, the 8th-gen iPad mini price has gone up, but there are some big changes. Apple says the refreshed 8th-gen iPad mini marks the most significant update ever for its petite tablet, featuring an OLED screen and the A20 Pro chip that we first saw in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. The new iPad mini has roughly the same footprint as the 2024 release, but the display is slightly larger thanks to a 24 percent reduction in bezel thickness. The device is almost a full millimeter thinner than the last iPad, coming in at just 5.4 mm. The chassis is also IP67 rated for water and dust protection. The 7th-Gen iPad mini didn't have any official IP rating. The 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display (up from 8.3 inches) moves on from the IPS technology of the last-gen device to adopt OLED. items.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
items.raw_text: Highway thieves are using sophisticated digital tactics that investigators worry make it easy to rob trucks carrying millions in expensive data center equipment. NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts yet and reported that since June, thieves have “made away with more than $100 million in data center freight.” Here’s how they said thieves get away with it: First, thieves hack freight brokers’ accounts on shipment-listing websites and post fake shipments to lure real bids, then send a malicious link to any trucking companies that respond. Once victims click, thieves install software to take control of their accounts and start bidding on real shipments. Sometimes, a real delivery driver is hired to collect the cargo, unaware of the scam, and other times fake driver’s licenses are used to get accomplices hired. Either way, the goods are eventually transferred to a driver working with the thieves to resell the gear, and, in one of the largest thefts, tracking coordinates were spoofed to prevent digital monitoring. items.title: Some iPhone Duo screens are already failing
items.raw_text: The iPhone Duo launched last week, offering anyone willing to spend $2,000 a chance to experience Apple's first foldable phone. For some early buyers, the morning after isn't going great. Despite the company's big talk about its "precision-engineered" hinge, some devices appear to have a hardware flaw that destroys the device's impressive internal display within hours (or minutes) of use. The Internet is currently overflowing with images of busted iPhone Duos, all sporting almost identical damage. The OLED is marred by several bright lines originating just below the midpoint of the display. These bands of damaged pixels extend all the way to the bottom and right edges. Some units also show lines of dead pixels following the crease from the top to the area where the bright lines begin. Anyone who has seen a damaged OLED panel will be familiar with this type of defect. When the layers of the display are damaged, the pixels no longer receive the correct voltage to illuminate them. Instead, they get the full driving voltage and are permanently on at maximum brightness. Some pixels can get no voltage, leaving them totally black. The only fix is to replace the OLED, but swapping the iPhone Duo's screen reportedly costs half as much as the device itself. Read full article Comments

Martje van Nes van Bibliotheek Schiedam koos ervoor het gesprek met de gemeente aan te gaan. Met hulp van Probiblio en het relevantiekader wist ze het gesprek te kantelen van producten en prestaties naar maatschappelijke waarde. In 2024 trad Martje van Nes aan als directeur van Bibliotheek Schiedam. Het was direct een uitdagende periode voor de subsidie van de bibliotheek. Hoe was de relatie met de gemeente bij jouw aantreden? “Het meerjarenbeleid van de bibliotheek én de termijn van het College kwamen tegelijk ten einde. Het was bekend dat er bezuinigd moesten worden maar het was nog onduidelijk wat de bezuinigingen precies voor de bibliotheek zouden betekenen. Ik had nog geen ervaring in het werken met gemeentelijke procedures, maar met die kennis is het achterhoofd was ik wel extra alert in het contact richting de gemeente, onze subsidieverstrekker.” In het gesprek met de gemeente stelde de ambtenaar voor met een producten- & dienstencatalogus te gaan werken. Ik vond het een goed idee om inzichtelijk te maken wat de bibliotheek bijdraagt aan de stad Schiedam. items.raw_text: Wat als je AI goedkoper kunt gebruiken én je de controle houdt over de informatie die je deelt? Bedrijven en organisaties die werken met AI-technologie kijken daarvoor met veel interesse naar open AI-modellen, die vooral door Chinese bedrijven worden gemaakt. Terwijl de grote Amerikaanse AI-bedrijven zoals Anthropic, OpenAI en Google abonnementskosten vragen en kosten rekenen voor het gebruik van hun krachtigste gesloten AI-modellen, zijn de open AI-modellen gratis te downloaden. Gebruikers kunnen daardoor zelf kiezen op welke servers een open AI-model draait, terwijl bij gesloten modellen de maker bepaalt. Dat kan risicovol zijn als je persoonlijke of gevoelige informatie wil verwerken met een gesloten AI-model: die gegevens worden verwerkt op computerapparatuur die je zelf niet beheert. De populairste open AI-modellen worden gemaakt door Chinese bedrijven zoals Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot en Z.ai. Ook een aantal Amerikaanse bedrijven brengt open AI-modellen uit, waaronder Meta, het bedrijf achter Facebook en Instagram. items.raw_text: In de aanloop naar de beursgang, de eerste van een groot ai-bedrijf, heeft Anthropic maandag zijn aanvraag voor een beursnotering ingediend. Naar het prospectus dat een blik werpt op het financiële reilen en zeilen van het bedrijf en de risico’s is maandenlang reikhalzend uitgekeken. Volgens Anthropic kan er met ai een hoop mis gaan. items.raw_text: NXP Semiconductors is een strategisch partnerschap aangegaan met de Volkswagen Group. Het beheren van deze functies via afzonderlijke elektronische regeleenheden (ecu’s) verhoogt de complexiteit van de ontwikkeling en het onderdelenbeheer. De schaalbaarheid wordt er bovendien door beperkt. items.title: SPN verkent hoe bibliotheken met leerecosystemen aan de slag kunnen
items.raw_text: Met het project Leerecosystemen werkt SPN aan een vertaling van het concept leerecosystemen naar de praktijk van bibliotheken en POI’s. Hoe kunnen bibliotheken vanuit bestaande samenwerkingen bijdragen aan een omgeving waarin mensen zich op hun eigen manier ontwikkelen? En hoe kunnen POI’s hen daarbij adviseren en ondersteunen? We kijken wat een leerecosysteem onderscheidt van andere vormen van samenwerking en wat bibliotheken en POI’s nodig hebben om ermee aan de slag te gaan. Het project wordt mogelijk gemaakt door subsidie van de KB en een eigen bijdrage van SPN. Wat verstaan we onder een leerecosysteem? Bibliotheken werken al jarenlang samen met scholen, gemeenten en maatschappelijke organisaties om inwoners te helpen zich te ontwikkelen. In dit verband spreekt de Netwerkagenda 2024–2027 over bloeiende, lokale netwerken waarin iedereen zich een leven lang kan ontwikkelen: leerecosystemen. Maar wat verstaan we precies onder een leerecosysteem? Waarom is het relevant? Wat zijn de kenmerken? Hoe verhoudt dit begrip zich tot bestaande werkwijzen, zoals integraal werken en netwerksamenwerking? Hoe raakt het aan de positie en rol van bibliotheken? Vanuit deze vragen onderzoekt SPN samen met de sector hoe bibliotheken invulling kunnen geven aan leerecosystemen, voortbouwend op bestaande kennis en ervaringen uit de praktijk.
